lessons.exercise: Change the activation shape to (17,257), freeze a NumPy random seed and compare two target-compatible block choices in interpretation. Keep the bias values distinct by column.
lessons.evidence: Broadcast/boundary checks, represented-input precision oracle and a tested no-fallback TPU guard; target execution remains separately unverified. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: What does a successful CPU interpret run establish for this target-oriented kernel?
lessons.hardware: CPU Pallas interpretation; actual TPU lowering and performance unverified

lessons.title: Tiling, memory, and pipelining
lessons.objective: Execute actual emit_pipeline semantics under explicit CPU TPU-layout simulation. Compare synchronous and buffered schedules against an independent oracle.
lessons.exercise: Use a (9,129) random fixture and verify synchronous, double-input-buffered and triple-input-buffered pipelines for both float32 and bfloat16 represented-input contracts. Keep output buffering at two slots.
lessons.evidence: Synchronous/buffered CPU simulation agreement, two/three input slots, unchanged output buffering, correctness across tiles and modeled footprint counts. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: The three-buffer simulation is correct and has fewer grid programs after a tile change. Can you conclude the TPU version is faster?
lessons.hardware: CPU Pallas interpretation; actual TPU lowering and performance unverified

lessons.title: Iterate with correctness and performance evidence
lessons.objective: Build a representative shape/dtype correctness matrix for an actual Pallas pipeline. Separate kernel implementation error from input/output precision differences.
lessons.exercise: Add a (15,255) fixture, compare two tile choices and two buffer counts, and retain the same frozen inputs for every candidate. Report errors and padded work separately.
lessons.evidence: Shape/dtype reference checks, separate precision gaps, guarded target benchmark and a bounded end-to-end speedup argument. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: The kernel matches the represented-input oracle exactly but differs from the original float32 dataset in bfloat16. What should the report say?
lessons.hardware: CPU Pallas interpretation; actual TPU lowering and performance unverified

phases.description: Write actual Pallas grids and buffered pipelines, verify boundaries and precision on CPU, and prepare guarded target measurements before claiming an optimization win.
phases.learningAdvice: Begin with a profiled operation and independent oracle. Complete CPU semantics first; actual TPU compilation, correctness and performance require the separate target runner on supported hardware.

studyGuide.question: Does a custom kernel earn its complexity?
studyGuide.why: A lower-level implementation first owes you the same numerical contract. Use hostile shapes, independent references and explicit target limits before attempting a speed claim.

readiness.prompt: A matrix dimension is not divisible by the tile size. What must the last tile do?
readiness.answer: Mask or pad out-of-range loads and stores under a declared policy. Valid elements still need exactly one correct output; fewer launched programs do not excuse missing boundary elements.

milestones.title: Prove indexing and arithmetic
milestones.task: Map each grid coordinate to input/output slices, test rectangular and boundary shapes and reject unsupported layouts or dtypes before launch.

milestones.title: Measure only a supported target
milestones.task: Check pipeline semantics and buffer assumptions, compare with a strong compiled baseline and make an end-to-end decision from the operation’s measured share.

transfer.prompt: Interpret mode passes all numerical tests. Can you use its timings to choose the fastest TPU tile?
transfer.approach: No. Interpretation supports bounded semantic checks. Compile and measure supported candidates on the named TPU with equivalent work and synchronization, including numerical verification there.

pitfall.symptom: A kernel passes square inputs but corrupts rectangular ones.
pitfall.check: Inspect operand-specific index maps and boundary masks; square dimensions can hide an axis swap.

studyGuide.completion: Use kernel-audit. Retain independent numerical checks, rejected unsupported contracts and a target measurement plan. Keep hardware timings unmeasured until actually executed.
studyGuide.furtherWork: Actual TPU/GPU compilation, race diagnosis and target tuning remain unqualified; CPU interpretation cannot close these gaps.

phases.title: Autodiff & JAX internals
phases.project: Audit derivatives and a tiny transformation
phases.checkpoint: Explain tracing and verify the derivative rule numerically.

lessons.title: Read your first jaxpr
lessons.objective: Inspect a small transformed function and identify its operations.
lessons.exercise: Change the scalar offset from 1 to 2. Draw the new value flow for [1, 2, 3], calculate the sum and gradient by hand, then inspect both jaxprs. Explain which structural features remain and which values change.
lessons.evidence: Save your annotated forward and derivative traces, offset-2 hand calculation, captured/explicit input comparison, unrolled/scan comparison and traced-branch error with both repaired numeric tests.
lessons.check: A jaxpr has more equations after grad. What can you conclude from that observation alone?

lessons.title: JVPs, VJPs, and higher-order derivatives
lessons.objective: Compute and interpret JVP and VJP products with correct domains and shapes. Verify the adjoint dot-product identity against a hand-derived Jacobian.
lessons.exercise: Repeat the Jacobian, JVP, VJP and adjoint checks at \(x=(-0.2,0.8)\) with \(v=(-0.5,1.3)\) and \(u=(1.1,-0.4)\). Explain which quantities belong to input and output space.
lessons.evidence: Hand-derived Jacobian/Hessian, adjoint scalar, changed-point checks, finite-difference HVP and a Gauss–Newton distinction. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: A VJP is seeded with an output weighting u. What does the returned input cotangent represent?

lessons.title: Custom derivative rules
lessons.objective: Implement actual custom_jvp and custom_vjp rules with correct return and residual contracts. Verify seed linearity, stable extreme values and second derivatives.
lessons.exercise: Check the custom log-sum-exp gradient on \((-3,0.2,2,5)\) against an independent stable softmax and central differences along two directions. Keep the output cotangent explicit.
lessons.evidence: Stable extreme inputs, analytic slopes/Hessians, seed linearity, independent finite differences and a deliberately wrong-rule diagnosis. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: A custom derivative is linear in its tangent and returns finite values. What additional evidence is necessary before calling it exact?

lessons.title: Lowering, compilation, and a tiny transformation
lessons.objective: Interpret literals, captured constants and variables in a supported flat jaxpr. Implement actual forward derivative rules without calling jax.jvp inside the interpreter.
lessons.exercise: Trace a new polynomial using only supported primitives, verify its interpreted derivative at two points, and compile that transformed computation independently.
lessons.evidence: Annotated primitive rules, constant/literal handling, independent expression oracles, changed compiled values and explicit unsupported/signature errors. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: Why does the tiny interpreter raise an error for an unsupported primitive instead of calling that primitive directly?

phases.description: Trace functions into jaxpr, check forward and reverse sensitivities, write exact custom derivatives and compile a small transformation with explicit supported primitives.
phases.learningAdvice: Keep an independent derivative reference and test changed values, higher derivatives and unsupported cases before trusting a transformation.

studyGuide.question: Which mathematical operation does the transformed program represent?
studyGuide.why: Use internal representations to explain and verify transformations, not to memorize printed variable names. Separate primal values, tangent directions, cotangents and compiled artifacts.

readiness.prompt: A function maps an input vector to an output vector. Does a JVP multiply by the Jacobian or its transpose?
readiness.answer: A JVP maps an input tangent through the Jacobian. A VJP maps an output cotangent through its transpose. Check the spaces and the adjoint inner-product identity.

milestones.title: Read and check transformed programs
milestones.task: Follow one jaxpr equation, compare directional derivatives independently and verify the adjoint identity at changed inputs.

milestones.title: Enforce a custom transformation boundary
milestones.task: Require tangent linearity and test higher-order promises. For the tiny interpreter, reject unsupported primitives rather than returning a plausible incomplete result.

transfer.prompt: A custom JVP returns the correct derivative when the tangent equals one but squares the tangent internally. Is it valid?
transfer.approach: No. Derivatives are linear maps in the direction at a fixed base point. Check multiple directions and linear combinations; agreement for one seed is insufficient.

pitfall.symptom: A derivative test passes at one input but fails after a shift.
pitfall.check: Inspect captured constants, detached values and custom rules. Compare both primal and derivative behavior at changed base points.

studyGuide.completion: Use derivative-audit. Keep analytic/directional checks, the adjoint identity, supported higher-order behavior and explicit unsupported-program rejections.
studyGuide.furtherWork: The tiny interpreter is intentionally incomplete. Production extension APIs, effects and full compiler transformation coverage require further targeted work.

phases.title: Deployment, interoperability & edge AI
phases.hardware: CPU for core labs; optional framework environments and target devices for conversion and edge validation
phases.project: Verify an inference artifact and capacity hypothesis
phases.checkpoint: Verify an exported prediction contract, report weight/activation precision error, and distinguish CPU request measurements from target-device evidence.

lessons.title: Adapt a pretrained model and choose a post-training objective
lessons.objective: Pretrain and reload an artifact with recorded data and checkpoint hashes Compare supervised adaptation and teacher distillation from the same starting weights
lessons.exercise: Adapt for zero steps and verify that predictions exactly match the reloaded checkpoint. Then run a short adaptation and show that the saved base is unchanged while the adapted parameters differ.
lessons.evidence: Source/checkpoint hashes, independent loss and gradient, disjoint evaluation results and teacher-failure diagnosis. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: Why should the two adaptation branches be compared using a common held-out criterion rather than their own training losses?

lessons.title: Move models between JAX, Keras, TensorFlow and PyTorch
lessons.objective: Verify parameter layouts and inference semantics before switching frameworks.
lessons.exercise: Add a batch with four rows and preserve the same parameters. Verify each row independently using a feature-by-feature sum.
lessons.evidence: Keep the layout map, two changed-input comparisons, runtime versions and optional backend-lab output. Identify which model state and preprocessing are not covered by a dense-layer match.
lessons.check: The Dense predictions match after transposing weights. What has been established?
lessons.hardware: CPU; optional framework and edge-device labs have separate requirements

lessons.title: Convert PyTorch weights to Flax and locate numerical errors
lessons.objective: Convert a real PyTorch state dictionary to Flax NNX and validate intermediate outputs, gradients and reloaded artifacts with explicit numerical tolerances.
lessons.exercise: Compare a near-zero reference against two candidate errors. Verify that the absolute tolerance accepts rounding noise but rejects a meaningful discrepancy.
lessons.evidence: Keep source checkpoint and architecture identity, complete parameter mapping, per-layer max-absolute/relative-L2 errors, elementwise tolerances, input-gradient comparisons, wrong-epsilon diagnosis and a fresh-process converted-artifact receipt.
lessons.check: The first linear layer agrees, but LayerNorm is the first mismatch. What should you inspect next?

lessons.title: Export a computation and verify its serving contract
lessons.objective: Round-trip an exported inference function and reject incompatible requests.
lessons.exercise: Verify a new input [-2, 0, 3] against an independent NumPy expression.
lessons.evidence: Keep the export/reload code, version/platform manifest, known-output and changed-input checks, rejected-shape result, and the planned serving request boundary.
lessons.check: What does a successful local export round trip prove?
lessons.hardware: CPU; optional framework and edge-device labs have separate requirements

lessons.title: Choose weight, activation and accumulation precision
lessons.objective: Compare floating-point policies, weight-only quantization and calibrated integer activations.
lessons.exercise: Add a zero-valued output channel and verify that its quantization scale is finite and its reconstruction is exactly zero.
lessons.evidence: Keep a precision table listing weight, activation, accumulator and output dtypes; max error and clipping counts on changed inputs; calibration provenance; and storage estimates that include scales and packing.
lessons.check: What must a deployment policy specify beyond “INT8 weights”?
lessons.hardware: CPU; optional framework and edge-device labs have separate requirements

lessons.title: Containerize a model service and verify its boundary
lessons.objective: Package an inference service and verify model identity, request validation and readiness across process and container boundaries.
lessons.exercise: Reject an artifact whose bytes changed after its expected digest was recorded.
lessons.evidence: Keep the artifact digest, valid and rejected requests, fresh-process output and, when Docker is available, the actual image identity, runtime user and container qualification receipt.
lessons.check: The image built successfully. What should happen before serving traffic?
lessons.hardware: CPU; Docker lab requires a local engine

lessons.title: Inference capacity, batching, and autoscaling
lessons.objective: Measure completed inference after warming each batch shape Report batch latency and example throughput with correct units
lessons.exercise: Simulate a burst of four requests arriving at time zero with a two-millisecond serial service duration. Derive all finish times and response times before executing.
lessons.evidence: Warm timing samples, latency/throughput units, independent queue timeline and labeled simulation/replica assumptions. Keep the environment, observed outputs and your explanation of the figure.
lessons.check: A batch of eight finishes in four milliseconds. Which statement follows for a fully occupied serial worker?

lessons.title: Deploy at the edge: conversion, budgets and device checks
lessons.objective: Define an edge runtime contract and measure an end-to-end batch-one request.
lessons.exercise: Send a second raw input [0, 255, 128] through the full request, and verify its independent normalized NumPy result.
lessons.evidence: Keep the CPU request report, preprocessing equivalence checks, chosen runtime/operator/precision matrix and an unfilled target-device report until actual device measurements exist. For the optional converter, retain the artifact, quantization metadata and held-out comparison.
lessons.check: A LiteRT file converts successfully. What must happen before claiming NPU latency?
lessons.hardware: CPU; optional framework and edge-device labs have separate requirements

phases.description: Adapt a trained model, verify framework and export contracts, compare precision policies and measure local inference before planning server or edge capacity. Package a model service in a reproducible container and verify readiness, artifact identity and request contracts.
phases.learningAdvice: Preserve checkpoint, data and calibration provenance. Compare held-out inputs before and after conversion; separate local request timing from queue simulation and target-device evidence.

studyGuide.question: Does the exported service preserve the model’s complete contract?
studyGuide.why: A deployment includes preprocessing, parameter layout, numeric policy and runtime behavior. Verify the same raw examples across each boundary before comparing memory or speed.

readiness.prompt: Weights match after conversion, but predictions differ. What besides weights must be compared?
readiness.answer: Compare input normalization, feature/channel order, operation semantics, non-trainable state, output labels, dtype and shape. Start with a hand-computed asymmetric example to expose layout mistakes.

milestones.title: Choose the model and preserve its meaning
milestones.task: Adapt the model under a fixed held-out protocol before freezing its release. Compare framework layouts, preprocessing and state with independent predictions. Convert the actual PyTorch model to Flax and locate an injected operation mismatch numerically. Keep a candidate decision table, feature/parameter mapping table, and the first divergent operation from a deliberately broken conversion.

milestones.title: Freeze the artifact and numeric policy
milestones.task: Export and load in a fresh process, reject malformed inputs, then track weight, activation, accumulator, bias and output formats. Separate clipping from rounding and retain held-out conversion checks. Include a fresh-interpreter export receipt, raw-request rejection cases, clipping counts and actual versus ideal packed byte counts.

milestones.title: Deliver to a stated runtime
milestones.task: Package and qualify the selected service, relate queue assumptions to measured service work, then examine the additional conversion and device budgets for an edge target. Leave actual device fields unmeasured until tested. Keep separate artifact, process, image and device receipts. Explain an interpolated percentile and a burst deadline failure before choosing a capacity intervention.

transfer.prompt: An INT8 model matches typical inputs but fails after a sensor’s range changes. How do you locate the regression?
transfer.approach: Verify raw preprocessing first; count values outside the frozen calibration range, inspect clipped channels and compare float-converted versus quantized outputs. Do not recalibrate on final test labels. Re-evaluate a revised policy on a separate held-out set.

pitfall.symptom: A smaller model file produces no lower request latency.
pitfall.check: Inspect load-time expansion, fallback operators, transfers and preprocessing on the named runtime. File size is not a kernel or latency measurement.

studyGuide.completion: Use deployment-audit and engineering-release to assemble one release dossier: candidate selection and retention criteria; a named feature and parameter mapping; source/export and layerwise parity; full precision policy and calibration identity; raw-request validation; artifact and process receipts; measured request samples; and a queue/deadline analysis. Mark container and target-device evidence unmeasured unless you actually ran those environments. Another learner should be able to reproduce each claimed check from the recorded inputs and command.
studyGuide.furtherWork: Actual edge-device delegates, thermal/energy budgets, packed low-bit kernels and production serving loads remain unqualified. The revised sequence moves adaptation before export and containerization before service capacity planning.

phases.title: Workload operations
phases.hardware: Executed local CPU processes; accelerator and cluster transfer require separate validation
phases.checkpoint: Diagnose a failed or stalled job, restore it correctly, and justify its resource plan from recorded measurements.

lessons.title: Accelerator jobs and runtime lifecycle
lessons.objective: Launch and reap a real bounded subprocess with explicit runtime requirements. Distinguish successful completion, worker failure and supervisor timeout.
lessons.exercise: Launch a changed job with \(3\) updates and batch size \(5\). Verify the observed progress steps and completion event rather than relying only on its exit code.
lessons.evidence: Keep actual child exit codes, bounded timeout/termination output and proof that children were reaped. Distinguish launch failure, failed preflight, slow work and a stalled job.
lessons.check: What must a timeout handler do beyond recording a timeout status?

lessons.title: Health, logs, and workload observability
lessons.objective: Build useful summaries from structured events emitted by a real worker. Define throughput with explicit numerator, denominator and synchronization boundary.
lessons.exercise: Compute the fraction of supervisor wall time spent inside synchronized updates, and state precisely what that fraction excludes.
lessons.evidence: Keep raw structured events, observed work counts, synchronized timing units and checkpoint lag. Derive job and update throughput with different boundaries.
lessons.check: What does update duty fraction establish in this lab?

lessons.title: Failure recovery and operational runbooks
lessons.objective: Rehearse a real worker failure and resume from an atomic complete-state checkpoint. Verify the next update and every later state against an uninterrupted reference.
lessons.exercise: Repeat the recovery drill with seed \(9\), checkpoint cadence \(3\) and failure after update \(5\). Verify restoration at step \(3\) and equality with a matching uninterrupted run.
lessons.evidence: Keep the injected failure timeline, accepted checkpoint identity and full-state comparisons for every resumed update. Record the incompatible and corrupted restore rejections.
lessons.check: Which evidence most directly supports a correct resume?

lessons.title: Changes, rollback, and artifact provenance
lessons.objective: Separate content identity, validation evidence and active selection. Reject corrupt or failed artifacts before a pointer change.
lessons.exercise: Publish two compatible validated artifacts that differ in an explicit release note. Activate both in sequence, then rollback and verify the exact selected ID and content.
lessons.evidence: Keep source/configuration/data hashes, actual held-out candidate predictions, the rejected degraded release and unchanged active pointer, followed by verified rollback.
lessons.check: What does a matching artifact digest establish?

lessons.title: Capacity, utilization, and operating cost
lessons.objective: Measure end-to-end local service time at more than one workload length. Compute offered load, worker reserve and illustrative cost with consistent units.
lessons.exercise: Using the measured service-time input, calculate the minimum worker count for \(1200\) arrivals per hour with \(40\)% reserve, then independently verify that the chosen count satisfies the load bound.
lessons.evidence: Keep measured job/update samples and independent unit calculations. Label demand, reserve and price assumptions as hypothetical before deriving a resource plan.
lessons.check: Which claim is supported by the measured update duty fraction?

lessons.title: MLOps: data contracts, CI gates and monitoring
lessons.objective: Reject data leakage and incomplete evaluation, compute count-weighted slice metrics and distinguish drift investigation from model promotion.
lessons.exercise: Show that averaging slice means without counts changes the overall error.
lessons.evidence: Keep the leaking-group rejection, data fingerprint, slice counts and MSEs, aggregate/slice gate disagreement, changed-population calculation and a written response to drift without labels.
lessons.check: An input drift alert fired before new labels arrived. What follows?

lessons.title: LLMOps: version prompts, evaluate behavior and trace requests
lessons.objective: Evaluate a versioned text application with a complete case inventory, slice-level answer contracts and inspectable MLflow traces.
lessons.exercise: Add a response with an invented citation and require the evaluator to fail it.
lessons.evidence: Keep all case IDs and per-slice replay scores, missing/duplicate-response rejections, the retained failed case, trace identities and application-version fields. Explain what requires separate live-model evaluation.
lessons.check: The controlled replay suite passes every case. What is established?

lessons.title: ModelOps: own, approve, roll back and retire a model
lessons.objective: Bind a release decision to immutable evidence, reject changed or expired approvals and preserve active selection after failure.
lessons.exercise: Change the evaluation hash while keeping the model unchanged, and prove the old approval no longer applies.
lessons.evidence: Keep the reviewed bundle hash, owner and target, expiry boundary, failed-transition pointer equality and changed-owner rejection. Explain why the local reviewer field is not authenticated approval.
lessons.check: An approval record contains a reviewer name and a matching hash. Does that authenticate the reviewer?

phases.description: Launch and observe real local jobs, detect failures and stalls, restore complete training state, verify artifact quality and rehearse rollback before planning capacity. Connect MLOps data/release gates, LLMOps evaluation/traces and ModelOps ownership/approval to the workload runbook.
phases.learningAdvice: Use a bounded failure drill and retain its raw event log. Check state and data identity before resuming; separate measured execution from hypothetical demand and pricing.

studyGuide.question: Can you detect, explain and safely recover a failed model release?
studyGuide.why: Operational evidence connects work done to user-visible behavior. Separate worker health, model quality and release ownership so an alert leads to a specific investigation rather than automatic retraining.

readiness.prompt: A worker process is alive but has emitted no progress for a long time. Is it healthy?
readiness.answer: Liveness only establishes that the process exists or responds. Check readiness, last completed work, expected duration and checkpoint freshness before choosing a bounded timeout or recovery action.

milestones.title: Observe and recover real work
milestones.task: Launch a bounded worker, retain structured events, rehearse a failure and verify the next restored update against uninterrupted work.

milestones.title: Control change and capacity
milestones.task: Reject invalid artifacts without changing selection. Revalidate rollback targets and calculate demand, reserve and cost with consistent measured units.

milestones.title: Connect MLOps, LLMOps and ModelOps
milestones.task: Use data and slice-quality gates, trace a versioned text application and bind review to the complete release bundle. Keep evaluator replay separate from live-model quality.

transfer.prompt: An input-distribution alert fires while delayed labels have not arrived. Should the system automatically retrain and promote?
transfer.approach: No conclusion about quality follows yet. Check data integrity, affected slices and service health; gather outcome evidence under a declared response policy. Any candidate must pass independent release gates, and selection must remain unchanged after failure.

pitfall.symptom: A release passes average error while a rare critical slice fails.
pitfall.check: Require per-slice counts and quality thresholds. Do not average slice means equally or treat a missing critical slice as a passing zero.

studyGuide.completion: Use workload-operations and engineering-release. Keep a real failure/recovery timeline, failed-gate invariance, a rollback drill, run/model identity and named review responsibilities.
studyGuide.furtherWork: Authenticated review, multi-writer promotion, staged cloud rollout, SLO alerting and live-model abuse evaluation still require separate infrastructure and application-specific labs.

phases.title: Self-supervised pretraining: masked and contrastive learning
phases.hardware: Executed CPU synthetic objectives; large-scale and human-feedback evaluation remain separate
phases.project: An audited pretraining and adaptation objective toolkit
phases.checkpoint: Complete stages 1–3 of training-methods with independent loss references, real training curves, changed masks or pairs and explicit synthetic-data limits.

lessons.title: Masked language modeling: predict hidden tokens
lessons.objective: Separate the clean targets from the corrupted input. Normalize over selected target positions.
lessons.exercise: Select the first position instead of the second and evaluate the trained model without updating it.
lessons.evidence: Keep corrupted inputs, selected-target counts, the log-vocabulary baseline, independent masked-loss checks, trained parameters and changed-mask results.
lessons.check: Why are visible input tokens useful even when their output positions are excluded from the loss?

lessons.title: Masked image modeling: reconstruct missing patches
lessons.objective: Preserve patch order and pixel order. Keep hidden pixels out of the encoder.
lessons.exercise: Verify the bottom-right patch against a direct slice and explain why a whole-array reshape can hide a spatial permutation.
lessons.evidence: Keep patch-order slices, visible-only feature shapes, hidden-patch counts, independent MSE and held-amplitude reconstruction results.
lessons.check: Why must the encoder input be inspected separately from reconstruction loss?

lessons.title: Contrastive learning: views, positives and negatives
lessons.objective: Define the positive pair before augmenting. Normalize embeddings and introduce temperature.
lessons.exercise: Permute only the right-hand embeddings after training and demonstrate the effect of broken pair identity.
lessons.evidence: Keep source pairing, temperature, stable two-direction loss checks, collapse and duplicate baselines, training outputs and broken-pair diagnosis.
lessons.check: What does successful retrieval on the training pairs establish?

phases.description: Train small masked-token, hidden-patch and paired-view models. Audit information leakage, reduction counts and pair identity before interpreting a falling objective.
phases.learningAdvice: Predict the mask, denominator or preference direction before training. Keep independent objective checks and changed-condition evidence.

studyGuide.question: What learning signal can unlabelled data provide?
studyGuide.why: Train small masked-token, hidden-patch and paired-view models. Audit information leakage, reduction counts and pair identity before interpreting a falling objective.

readiness.prompt: If an image reconstruction is perfect before training, what boundary should you inspect?
readiness.answer: Check whether hidden pixels entered the encoder or were copied into the prediction. A valid objective can still be defeated by leaked inputs.

milestones.title: Masked language modeling: predict hidden tokens
